title: Slice and trim: drop what no target rests on; prove only what the outgoing edges demand for B.15 and 4.5

add.label: Proposition B.15'
add.name: Running time of the reductions, O-form
add.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 5.9, if $\mathcal{A}$ runs in time $t$ and makes at most $Q_H$ queries to each of $H_{\mathsf{seed}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{key}}$, then $\mathcal{B}_0$ and $\mathcal{B}_1$ run in time at most $t_R = t + O(Q + d_R\, Q_H + \mu) + \mathsf{poly}(D, \log q)$.
add.proof:
Let $\mathcal{B}_b$ sample the coins of (R2) first and follow the calls as $\mathcal{A}$ makes them, with tables of labels, exponents, records, rejected strings, names and oracle answers; by Lemma B.14(a) this changes no output. Count its operations beyond the time $t$ of $\mathcal{A}$ in four groups; write $N' := N + 1$.
(i) Calls to $\mathcal{O}_{\mathsf{GG}}$. A call has one result and at most two operand strings. Answering it takes a bounded number of table lookups and insertions, one exponent, one value at $\mathsf{a}_{\mathrm{p}}$ for the record of (R3), one label, one name, and, for each operand string not yet in a table, one decision whether it is a label, one sampled exponent and one record of $0$: $O(1)$ operations. For (R4), at each of the six recovery points $\mathcal{B}_b$ extends the straight-line computation of the exponents by the $O(1)$ operations of this call, and for each of the at most two expressions of (R3) computes its gradient in $r$ backwards through that computation, at $O(1)$ operations for each operation of it [Baur and Strassen, Theorem 2]. So the $Q$ calls cost $O(Q)$.
(ii) Oracle queries. A query to $H_{\mathsf{key}}$ is a lookup, a sample and an insertion. A query to $H_{\mathsf{seed}}$ samples the $d_R$ coefficients of one element of $R_q$ and makes a lookup and an insertion. So the queries cost $O(d_R\, Q_H)$.
(iii) Work that does not depend on $\mathcal{A}$. By the specification of $\mathsf{Enc}$ the number $L$ of received labels is $O((K_1 + K_2) N' + D + n (J + J'))$. The exponents of all published elements are evaluated at eight points, the coins of $\mathsf{Enc}$ and the seven points of (R2); one evaluation computes $z$ at its three points from $M$ in $O(k\, d_R\, N')$ operations, the $2N' + 3$ polynomials $A_i$, $B_i$, $Z$, $Z_0$, $L_\rho$ at $\tau$ by Horner's rule from their coefficients in $O(N' D)$, the scalars of the legs and cells in $O(n)$, the masks in $O(K_2 N')$, and then $O(1)$ operations for each published element. Entering the received labels takes $O(L)$. Placing the challenge and answering the $k(\ell + 1)$ seed queries of $\mathsf{Enc}$ takes $O(k \ell + k\, d_R)$, and the masked message $O(\mu)$. After the run, for each of the at most two expressions, the gradients are reduced to two echelon forms of three vectors of $\mathbb{F}_q^{N'}$ in $O(N')$, intersected with the kernel of $z$ in both sectors in $O(k\, d_R\, N')$, and one vector is packed in $O(N')$. The description of $\mathcal{B}_b$ beyond that of $\mathcal{A}$ holds the $O(N' D)$ coefficients of those polynomials, the evaluation points, $m_b$ and code of constant length: $O(N' D + \mu)$. Now $k\, d_R < n \le D$ and $N < D$; $K_1 K_2 = n/2$ gives $K_1, K_2 \le n$; $k \ell \le k (N + d_R) < n N'$; and $J \le J\Delta \le D + n \le 2D$ by (P1) while $J' \le \max\{n_{\mathsf{c}}, 1\} \le D$. Hence every term of this group is $O((N + n) D + \mu)$.
(iv) $\mathsf{LIFT}$ is run at most twice, once for each expression of (R3), and each run takes time polynomial in $N$ and $\log q$ by Lemma B.9.
In total $\mathcal{B}_b$ runs in time at most $t + O(Q) + O(d_R\, Q_H) + O((N + n) D + \mu)$ plus two runs of $\mathsf{LIFT}$, which is $t + O(Q + d_R\, Q_H + \mu) + \mathsf{poly}(D, \log q)$, as $N < D$ and $n \le D$.
add.explain: The running time of the two reductions without explicit constants: linear in the adversary's calls and queries, plus a polynomial that does not depend on the adversary.

add.label: Lemma 4.5'
add.name: Rank bound, inequality only
add.proof:
(a) Let $M$ be the matrix of all rows of all $W_c$, of rank $d := \operatorname{rank} \mathbf{W}$, and fix $u$. Choose $d$ linearly independent columns of $M$, column $0$ among them unless it is zero. Given the entries of $r$ at the other indices in $[N]$, at most one value modulo $q$ of its entries at the chosen indices solves $M r = u$. Each of the independent entries $r_1, \dots, r_N$ takes a given value modulo $q$ with probability at most $1/g$, as $g + 1 < q$; so does $r_0$ given all of them. Hence $\Pr[M r = u] \le g^{-d}$, as in Odlyzko's lemma \cite[Lemma 3.1]{NW22}.
(b) Write $v = \sum_c W_c^\top z_c$. Then $v^\top r = \sum_c z_c^\top W_c r$ is a function of $(W_c r)_c$, so it takes one value whenever $(W_c r)_c$ takes its likeliest value, and $\operatorname{gp}(v^\top) \ge \operatorname{gp}(\mathbf{W})$.
add.explain: A stack of rank d is guessed with probability at most g^(-d), and a vector of its row space is at least as easy to guess as the stack.

edges.demand: Sampling the reduction's coins before the run changes no output.

edges.demand: T_(LIFT) is polynomial in N and log q.
The gradient of a computation costs a constant number of operations per operation of the computation.

discharge.argument: The demand asks that B_0 and B_1 run within t_R = t + O(Q + d_R Q_H + mu) + poly(D, log q). The new statement is that bound, under the same hypotheses; s_b <= Adv^MSIS(t_R) then holds by the definition of Adv^MSIS(t_R) in the corollary.

The demand asks for the inequality gp(W) <= g^(-rank W) of part (a), so that rank >= 4 gives gp <= g^(-4) < theta, and for part (b), gp(v^T) >= gp(W) for v in the row space. Both are parts (a) and (b) of the new statement, word for word.
